content.text: ## Bangles del Águila _aka, "Navajo Bracelets"; aka, "Beautiful Corded Leather Turquoise Fractal Bangles"_ **San Jaya Prime**, _Southwestern Symbol Fractals_ This right here? It's one of my top-five selling designs of all time -- especially when it's slapped onto a throw pillow. It's also a massive piece of the puzzle in my award-winning _[Egyptian Turquoise](queen-of-the-nile)_ series, built alongside visionaries like TINY BLVCK, iMeena, and Arike. Wait strike that whole "one of my top-five" <- it's THE top, my #1 top-selling design. Ever. I just checked the numbers and nothing else comes close. The roots of this symbol fractal dig deep into my time out in Santa Fe, Taos, and the high deserts of Northern Arizona. I spent entire summers -- even weathering a few brutal winter months -- living with the Jicarilla Apache and the Navajo. The endless, meticulous hours they pour into their crafts... especially the jewelry and the weaving... it completely changes how you see art. And their use of turquoise? _Absolutely striking!_ I can almost hear Pops chiding me and saying I'd burn myself with the way I was holding the heat in my hands to work the silver. Some lessons have to be learned the hard way. Whenever I look at this piece, it rips me right back to those days. Suddenly, I'm sitting in the back of a pickup truck with Mario and his sons... buffalo running wild right alongside the tires... and nothing but a wide-open horizon stretching out in absolutely every direction. \[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23570205)\] Also available on Redbubble in: [bronze + tan](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/24241553), [blue + gold](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/42029652), [red + black](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23570597), [black + stars](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/20970067), [black on white](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/24249422), [teal + pink](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/31875906), [beige + seafoam](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/55844270) PS: In the photo above, you can see the original design (along with the bronze + tan) on my bed at "The Reliquary" -- my last apartment in the city of Las Vegas. Those particularly beautiful pillows went to Doc Dillon when I left the city.

content.text:
## The Cost of Bad Burglars

I'm a thief myself. I come from the streets and I've taken from others in mashups, DJ sets, stole Joker for a mascot, and have never paid a dime for that shit. I get it! But there are good thieves who make quality shit and then there are the idiots. With "Bangles del Aguila" being my most stolen design, along with my best seller, I'm only going to do a breakdown like this once -- right here and now! -- as an example of what goes on.

If you've bought art from the Amazon store or even off of Walmart, no matter the supposed artist, it was most likely stolen. That's just the tip of the iceberg. The idiots and bad burglars among the lot don't even change the title of the designs. Seriously! They straight rip the art, the title, then just re-post it online to see if anyone bites.

That makes it very easy to track those down.

There are thousands of my own right now on Amazon and hundreds on Walmart. There's literally professional rip-off sites out there like Pinterval, AliExpress, Desertcart, and Shop App (just to name a few) that do nothing BUT this rip-and-sell model.

If they were selling high quality products, and somehow beating my prices, I'd actually be impressed. I'd want to know how they were doing it and I'd take a gander at who their manufacturers were. But they're not. When the products actually arrive, they're cheap, sometimes already faded, and they fall apart quickly.

Then here's where the real problem begins, because that shit reflects on me and my art. It's my art they've stolen, and when it falls apart the fools who fell for the low-end thieves out there believe that it's on me. I know, because I've heard from them. Nah, y'all, that shit ain't on me. I carefully source fabrics, with my favorite out of Montreal, Canada, and constantly do quality checks with the stores that I sell through. That's how Redbubble and Zazzle became my primary outlets to get my art out there into the world.

My friend Jeff even turned me on to the fact that this is happening with big, well-known channels like Nerdforge ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qh2RN4pDga4)). Now here's the thing: that means Amazon and Walmart are intentionally allowing this. Amazon especially has no excuse, since they constantly leverage AI, which can pinpoint the true artist behind a design. Even in my case, pre-AI there was a simple Google search where the title itself would already lead back to me. By allowing it, they're supporting it.

Instead of linking to anything, instead I'll just grab screenshots to illustrate some quick searches.

## Bespoke, Custom, Quality Designs

You can see one of my custom kimonos with "Bangles del Águila" here on the right and immediately tell the design apart from the thieves. Everything was placed with intention, the design itself all comes from quality sources, and displayed with my own signature on it. For this and other custom designs, [contact me](contact).

I have too many friends who live off their art... who are constantly being undercut by thieves selling off cheap, low-quality fakes. With the big online stores actively supporting the thieves, that means they need to go through the long, arduous process of issuing DMCA strikes... one thief at a time. I should know, I've filled out a little over 2,000 of them in my lifetime.

Google, Amazon, Walmart -- _all of them!_ -- they could have a single registry, to submit your art, including each name it's known by, then with example merchandise along with a list of links. That one registry should act as a single source of truth. But again, as I said earlier, that's not even needed. They already have the tech to do this on their own. They've _chosen_ to do the minimum to force artists to go through this long process, putting it on the artist... instead of programming it _themselves_ into _their_ stores.

It's not AI that I'm worried about as an artist; it's humans.

In fact, in thanks to AI, I've already started tracking these. I'll soon be automating the takedown notices, having Mycroft handle the forms and issuing them. For this particular design, I've been hunting the thieves since 2011 when I first released it. Soon I'll have all my top-sellers being tracked and handled by AI to go through and eliminate the thieves on my behalf since the larger online stores won't do it for me.

That only solves this for me. Then I'll turn my resources towards helping my friends in the community. This has gone on long enough.

Until then, however, [contact me](contact) for custom requests or buy solely on my official Redbubble store ([link](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23570205)).

To my fellow artists: When you first discover the thieves, many feel a gut reaction to pull everything you've published and delete it. _"Take it all down!"_ Don't! You need that evidence! You need the pages and the proof that you were online first. If it's been stolen, then it's already out of your reach and you'll need every weapon you can muster to take down the fakes. So don't go scorched earth on it. Take a step back, breathe... then start loading bullets into the chamber.
